payload.title: What Are the German Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.excerpt: Polterabend, log sawing, the veil dance and the Standesamt: German wedding traditions by when they happen, and what Australian couples should check.
payload.author: Wedded Wonderland
key_takeaways: In Germany, only the declaration before the registrar at the Standesamt creates a legal marriage, so the civil ceremony comes first.
The Polterabend is a noisy pre-wedding party where guests smash porcelain, never glass, and the couple sweep up the shards together.
Many reception customs, from sawing a log together to the veil dance, are playful rituals the guests join in.
Customs vary by region, so treat them as a menu to choose from with your family rather than a checklist.

faq.q: What do German brides traditionally wear?
faq.a: Today most wear white, but the long white dress only became generally accepted in Germany in the 1930s. Before that, rural brides wore a black festive dress with a white veil.

faq.q: Which hand do Germans wear their wedding ring on?
faq.a: The right hand, for both partners. An engagement ring is generally worn on the left and moved to the right after the ceremony, or no longer worn.
Guests smash porcelain or stoneware, never glass, for luck, and the couple sweep up the shards together. It is now usually held at least a week before the wedding.

faq.q: Do you have to marry at the Standesamt in Germany?
faq.a: Yes, for a legal marriage. As at November 2026, the German Civil Code says a marriage is concluded only by the couple's declaration before the registrar. A church or celebrant ceremony can follow as the celebration.

faq.q: What should you wear to a German wedding as a guest?
faq.a: Follow the invitation and the couple's lead. Customs vary by region, and we found no source for a national guest dress code.

faq.q: What do guests give at a German wedding?
faq.a: Ask the couple or their families, as gift customs vary by region. Some reception games, such as the money variant of the veil dance, collect cash for the newlyweds.
